cards.title: Iran and Oman sketch a temporary navigation corridor for Hormuz
cards.summary: Iran and Oman discussed a phased framework for ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, including a temporary corridor and joint mine-clearance work, while the waterway remains largely shut.
detail: The Associated Press reported that Oman’s foreign minister met Iran’s foreign minister in Tehran on Aug. 25 to discuss a framework for managing ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. A joint statement described a proposed temporary navigational corridor and a joint project to clear mines.

The practical stakes are immediate for shipping, energy markets, and states on both sides of the waterway. The proposal is a framework for further technical talks, not evidence that normal traffic has resumed; AP also reported that an oil tanker had been disabled in an attack off Oman.

The next check is whether technical negotiations produce operating rules, whether mine-clearance work begins, and whether ships can pass safely. The parties’ understanding of the corridor’s route and future administration remains subject to negotiation.

cards.title: EU approves €6.1 billion in defence procurement for Ukraine
cards.summary: The European Commission approved a new Ukraine defence-procurement package for air defence, missiles, ammunition, and radars under the €90 billion support loan.
detail: The European Commission said on Aug. 24 that it approved €6.1 billion in new defence procurement for Ukraine. The package covers air and missile defence systems, missiles, ammunition, and radars and forms part of the Ukraine Support Loan for 2026–27.

The decision turns a broad political commitment into a procurement mechanism: Ukraine can request payments against contracts with defence companies, while the Commission reviews those contracts before disbursement. The Commission said the new approval brings already approved procurement plans to €16 billion, with €8.35 billion disbursed from those plans.

The unresolved question is delivery speed. The Commission linked the decision to intensified missile and drone attacks and said production, destocking, and order reprioritisation must increase. The announced funding is verified; its battlefield effect depends on contracts, manufacturing, and delivery.
